Integrate a calibration offset along a grid coordinate

Source: R/marginal.R
jitter_marginal.Rd

Several assays can measure the same underlying gain on scales that do not quite agree. Rather than give each assay its own class coordinate, which would stop them speaking to the same question, the shared coordinate is read with an assay-specific offset: assay \(t\) sees \(g + w\delta_t\), and the offset is integrated out with equal weight.

Usage

jitter_marginal(E, n_grid, keep, offsets, weights = NULL)

Arguments

E

A participant-by-column matrix whose columns are the grid coordinate (running fastest) crossed with any number of other coordinates.

n_grid

The length of the grid coordinate, which must divide ncol(E).

keep

Integer indices into seq_len(n_grid) to retain: the interior sub-range on which the result is reported.

offsets

Integer offsets, in grid steps, to average over. Every keep + offsets must lie inside the grid, which is checked.

weights

Optional weights on offsets; equal by default.

Value

A matrix with length(keep) times the other coordinates' columns, the grid coordinate still running fastest.

Details

This requires the likelihood on a wider grid than the one kept, so that every shifted read stays inside it. That is why the design has an outer grid and an interior shared sub-range: keep indexes the latter within the former.

See also

pool_marginal().

Examples

E <- matrix(log(c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5)), nrow = 1)
jitter_marginal(E, n_grid = 5, keep = 2:4, offsets = c(-1, 0, 1))
#>           [,1]     [,2]     [,3]
#> [1,] 0.6931472 1.098612 1.386294
